newsitem.title: JAPAN: NTT cell phone unit mulls abolishing joining fees.
newsitem.headline: NTT cell phone unit mulls abolishing joining fees.

text.p: Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp's cellular phone unit, the NTT DoCoMo group, said on Wednesday it is considering abolishing initial subscription fees of 4,500 to 6,000 yen in a bid to attract more customers.
"It is one of several measures being considered," said an NTT DoCoMo spokesman.

The Nihon Keizai Shimbun business daily reported earlier that the group is preparing to seek government approval to abolish the fees by December. DoCoMo provides services nationwide through nine regional companies and currently has a total of eight million subscribers, the company spokesman said.
The number of subscribers is increasing by about 500,000 a month, the spokesman said.
When NTT started the cellular phone service in 1979, a new subscriber was charged 80,000 yen as the initial fee. But this has fallen sharply since 1991 amid intensifying competition.
But even if the initial fee is dropped, the firm plans to continue charging 3,000 yen as a handling fee to new subscribers.

An industry organisation, Telecommunications Carriers Association, reported last month that the total number of subscribers for mobile phones and car phones in Japan reached 15.31 million at the end of September.
